title: Have and Has
introduction: Practise have and has with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: Have and has help us talk about possessions and features.
rules: Use have with I, you, we and they. Use has with he, she, it and a single person or thing.
Use have and has for belongings, family relationships and animal features.
When asking with does, use have: Does she have a pencil?

grammar.description: Do you have a ruler? Does she have a book?

examples.question: Ask whether Ali owns a kite.
Complete: My sister ___ a blue bag.

exercises.question: A bird ___ wings.
exercises.solution: A bird is singular, so use has.

exercises.question: The cat ___ whiskers.
exercises.solution: The cat is singular, so use has.

exercises.question: My cousins ___ bicycles.
exercises.solution: Cousins is plural, so use have.

exercises.question: Does he ___ a ruler?
exercises.solution: After does, use the base form have.

exercises.question: Do they ___ books?
exercises.solution: After do, use the base form have.

exercises.question: The house ___ two doors.
exercises.solution: The house is singular, so use has.

exercises.question: Ali and Mei ___ lunch boxes.
exercises.solution: Two people joined by and form a plural subject.

summary: Have and has help us talk about possessions and features.
